newsitem.title: MEXICO: Natural gas to fuel more Mexican vehicles -assn.
newsitem.headline: Natural gas to fuel more Mexican vehicles -assn.

text.p: Mexican industrial and mass transport vehicles will increasingly convert to natural gas fuel in the coming months, the Mexican Natural Gas Association said Thursday.

"Soon we will have important advances in the use of natural gas for vehicles...in about eight months," Alejandro Maldonado Moreno, the association's vice president for vehicle natural gas, told reporters.

Three years of tests have shown that natural gas use reduces contaminants by 96 percent, he said. Chronic smog problems in Mexico's largest cities have been partly attributed to the quantity of cars and to leaded gasolines.
Natural gas is not expected to fuel the average family car, however, because of the high cost of converting vehicles to natural gas and the limited supply centers of natural gas.
Maldonaldo said converting vehicles from using gasoline to natural gas has been reduced from $4,000 per auto to $3,500.
New Mexican Gas Association President Angelica Fuentes also said the organization is studying ways to help regulate natural gas prices.

Domestic natural gas hit five-year high prices in December, at $3.73 per million British Thermal Units (BTUs). For February, state oil and gas monopoly Petroleos Mexicanos (Pemex) reduced prices 30 percent, and Fuentes said prices are expected to drop another 25 percent.
"The association is undergoing a study to see mechanisms and instruments to protect consumers from these types of fluctuations because of demand," Fuentes said, declining to provide further details.
Natural gas is primarily used industrially in Mexico, although the government is encouraging the cleaner fuel rather than the common domestic liquid petroleum gas (LPG).
